source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Usage/UsageViews.swift:293-307 private func spend(_ row: BankedResetRowModel) { phase = .applying(row.id); settle?.cancel(); settle = Task { do { let outcome = try await model.providers.consumeResetCredit(provider, row.credit?.id); phase = .done(outcome) } catch { phase = .failed(error.localizedDescription) }; try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(4)); guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }; phase = .idle } }

requirements.expected_result: The phase becomes applying for that row, any previous settle task is cancelled, and a new task calls consumeResetCredit with the provider and the credit's id, which is nil for a placeholder row. On success the phase becomes done carrying the outcome; on a thrown error it becomes failed carrying the error's localized description. Either way the task then sleeps four seconds and, unless cancelled, returns the phase to idle. The four second hold applies to both success and failure.
side_effects: Calls the provider through the registry; for Codex this runs the CLI's app-server consume call, for Z.ai its reset-card endpoint.
